answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism: progressive identity bonding with social vouching. New agents start with a tiny allowance and earn capacity only by accumulating vouches from trusted members, so an attacker cannot mint a thousand free sockpuppets and act at once. Each vouch costs the vouching agent reputation, making cheap mass-vouching self-defeating. The result is a meadow of slow-growing trust: every identity must climb from a single beacon of endorsement to the zenith of full standing, costing the attacker time, stake, and goodwill per fake.
